# Devir algoritmo: usos do CHAT-GPT em aulas de argumentação

## DOI:

https://doi.org/10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399
## Resumo

O educador cubano José Martí nos convoca a “conhecer as forças do mundo” a fim de “fazê-las trabalhar”, ao invés de apenas valorar as mudanças como boas ou más. As Inteligências Artificiais (doravante IA) são, sem dúvida, uma das “forças” do contemporâneo. Há, no entanto, muito a ser debatido e compreendido ainda. Dentre as tecnologias de IA, as assim chamadas inteligências artificiais gerativas, como o Chat-GPT, têm se tornado cada vez mais populares no ambiente acadêmico. Diante desse cenário e das reflexões desenvolvidos na GrupA – Grupo de Práticas em Semântica e Discurso (UFBA/CNPq), passei a me perguntar sobre os modos de construir o programa de uma disciplina que ministro para os cursos de Letras da Universidade Federal da Bahia - *Estratégias Argumentativas em Língua Portuguesa*. Esse questionamento, unindo preocupações de ensino e de pesquisa, me conduziu à construção da sequência didática que ora apresento e discuto nesse artigo, e que apliquei durante dois semestres consecutivos no ano de 2023. Junto às práticas pedagógicas de Paulo Freire, retomamos diferentes autores a fim de construir essa sequência didática em quatro etapas: a) tematização; b) problematização; c) avaliação; e d) transvaloração. As conclusões do artigo discutem a precarização dos letramentos das classes trabalhadoras no capitalismo algorítmico, ao passo que apontam a possibilidade de produzir fissuras no ritual ideológico.

## Overview of Long-Context Generative AI Models

Long-context models refer to generative artificial intelligence technologies—such as variants of the ChatGPT/GPT architecture mentioned in academic and pedagogical discourse—that are increasingly utilized to process, analyze, and generate text across diverse applications [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399]. While platforms like ChatGPT have become prominent tools within academic environments for studying argumentative strategies and textual production, they operate as automated linguistic forces within contemporary algorithmic capitalism [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399]. 

## Handling Longer Input Sequences

Generative AI models process extensive input sequences by leveraging complex computational structures that manage linguistic data, enunciation spaces, and semantic framing [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399]. In educational and analytical contexts, these tools parse large volumes of text—ranging from prompts to entire pedagogical frameworks—by drawing upon foundational principles of machine learning and natural language processing [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399]. The integration of such technologies into structured sequences allows users to evaluate, problematize, and interact with extensive textual inputs, maintaining coherence across extended dialogues or documents [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399].

## Open Questions

* What specific architectural modifications (e.g., attention mechanism scaling, memory augmentation) do proprietary long-context models employ to maintain retrieval accuracy over extended sequences, and how do they compare empirically?
* How do varying input lengths impact the ideological or argumentative fidelity of generative outputs in specialized academic applications?
* *To settle these questions:* Controlled benchmarking studies evaluating retrieval-in-context performance alongside qualitative discourse analyses of long-form generation are required.

## Practical Takeaways

* **Incorporate with Critical Frameworks:** When utilizing generative AI tools for analyzing extended texts or argumentative strategies, combine the technology with pedagogical frameworks (such as thematic structuring, problematization, and evaluation) to maintain critical oversight [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399].
* **Acknowledge Systemic Limitations:** Recognize that algorithmic text generation operates within specific socio-technical constraints; educators and researchers should treat outputs as conversational and analytical drafts rather than neutral authorities [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399].
* **What to Try First:** Begin by applying generative models to bounded, step-by-step didactic sequences (e.g., analyzing specific segments of an argument) before scaling up to massive input sequences, ensuring that the model's contextual adherence can be closely monitored [^crossref:10.28998/2317-9945.202483.384-399].
